Identify the **Longest Edge Propagation Path (LEPP)** starting from $T$ [S1, unofficial].

The claim asks to identify the Longest Edge Propagation Path (LEPP) starting from triangle T. The provided evidence explicitly defines LEPP in the context of the ROAM algorithm. Specifically, the notes and passages state that to split triangle T, one must 'recursively split all required triangles along the longest edge path until a terminal edge is found'. It further clarifies that this path involves forcing neighbors (like Tb) to split first to avoid cracks, and that the process finishes when a terminal edge (base edge for two adjacent triangles or border edge) is found. The evidence fully supports the description and identification of the LEPP as the recursive path of splits required to maintain mesh consistency when splitting a triangle.

The LEPP mechanism ensures $T_b$ is split first, propagating the refinement to maintain continuity [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that if a triangle T is split while its base neighbor Tb is of a coarser level, it would produce a crack. To prevent this, 'Tb must be forced to split first,' which triggers a recursive process known as the Longest Edge Propagation Path (LEPP). This process ensures that the refinement propagates to maintain mesh continuity.
